---
title: "Running Rill for others"
---

On your own machine, Rill trusts whoever runs it and serves one Library.
Hosting it adds three jobs: signing people in, keeping feeds fresh without
anyone having the app open, and knowing when something breaks.

## Choosing a host

The repository documents two setups. Both keep all state in PostgreSQL, so the
app itself can restart or move freely.

- Posit Connect Cloud, with Auth0 sign-in inside the app
  (`RILL_IDENTITY_MODE=auth0`). The
  [Connect Cloud runbook](https://github.com/JamesHWade/rill/blob/main/docs/deployment/connect-cloud.md)
  covers the manifest, the Auth0 application, Neon, and hourly polling from
  GitHub Actions.
- A Docker image that runs Rill behind oauth2-proxy
  (`RILL_IDENTITY_MODE=oidc_proxy`), with a separate cron job for polling. The
  [Render guide](https://github.com/JamesHWade/rill/blob/main/docs/deployment/render.md)
  covers the image, a local Docker Compose setup, and the environment.

## Admitting readers

The people listed in `RILL_ALLOWED_OIDC_SUBJECTS` sign in to the Library that
belongs to `RILL_ACTOR_ID`. When anyone else signs in, Rill records an access
request, tells them to wait for approval, and shows them nothing else.

The reader who signs in to `RILL_ACTOR_ID`'s Library sees **Access requests**
in the sidebar and can approve requests there. An operator with the
deployment's `DATABASE_URL` can do the same from R:

```r
requests <- rill::list_reader_admissions()
rill::approve_reader_admission(
  requests$request_id[[1]],
  responsible_id = "operator:james"
)
```

Each approval creates a new, empty Library, and approving the same request
again changes nothing. Readers share feed downloads and public article copies.
Subscriptions, Groups, reading state, captured pages, ratings, and memories
stay private to each reader. Requests that nobody approves expire 30 days after
the person's last sign-in.

## Keeping feeds fresh

`poll_feeds()` checks each feed that at least one reader follows once its
interval has passed (`RILL_POLL_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, 60 by default). It skips the
run if another poll is still going, records the result for every feed, and
backs off feeds that keep failing, from one hour up to one day. It exits with
an error when `RILL_POLL_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` feeds fail (5 by default). After
polling, it prepares up to 100 recent full articles.

Schedule `Rscript scripts/poll.R` to run it. The repository's **Poll feeds**
GitHub Actions workflow runs it hourly once you set the repository variable
`RILL_POLLING_ENABLED` to `true` and store the database URL in the
`RILL_DATABASE_URL` secret.

Readers can refresh from the app at any time. Set `RILL_REFRESH_ON_START=true`
to refresh whenever someone opens it.

## Telemetry

Rill sends OpenTelemetry traces and logs to any OTLP endpoint, such as
Logfire, Grafana Cloud, or Honeycomb. These settings export only Rill's own
spans and suppress the automatic spans from httr2, ellmer, and deputy, which
can contain URLs and conversation text:

```text
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=rill
OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.namespace=personal-reader,deployment.environment=production
OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=http
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=http
OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none
OTEL_R_EMIT_SCOPES=rill
OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES=httr2,ellmer,deputy
OTEL_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT=256
OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=false
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://logfire-us.pydantic.dev
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=Authorization=your-logfire-write-token
```

Rill's spans record timings, counts, and error classes. They leave out article
titles and text, full URLs, reader and story identifiers, and exception
messages. The traces worth knowing:

- `article.open` follows a story from the click to readable text.
  `reading.first_text_ms` is measured in the browser.
- `queue.action` times mark-read, save, and Undo from the click to the update
  on screen.
- `article.prepare` covers background extraction: `queue.wait_ms`,
  `worker.bootstrap_ms`, and an `article.extract.http` span with the HTTP
  status. A failure carries the same reference that the app shows the reader.
- `orientation.maintain` covers Orientation updates.
  `orientation.failure_stage` says where an update failed, and `error.classes`
  lists up to eight nested error classes.

## Reading history

Rill records reading activity in the `events` table of your database: stories
opened and where they were opened from, scroll and reading-time milestones,
stars, saves, read-state changes, Orientation dismissals, captures, and changes
to feeds and Groups. These records stay in your database. Rill doesn't send
them to telemetry or to model providers.
